2026-08-25T03:26:45.4826579Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4826996Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4827363Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4827899Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4828369Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4828941Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4830589Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4832738Z >
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4835297Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4837957Z >
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4838856Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4839714Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4839927Z ### How to Use
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4840199Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4841152Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4842089Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4842311Z ```bash
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4842953Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4843792Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4844517Z ```
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4844758Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4845074Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4845706Z ```bash
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4846323Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4847207Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4848170Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4849005Z ```
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4849240Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4849925Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4851075Z ```bash
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4851738Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4852501Z ```
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4852747Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4853281Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4853990Z ```bash
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4854634Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4855651Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4856444Z ```
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4856682Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4856990Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4857489Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4859027Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4860954Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4861174Z ```bash
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4861708Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4862707Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4863637Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4863996Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4864521Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4865635Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4866569Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4867112Z ```
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4867348Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4868163Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4869178Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4869381Z ```bash
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4870145Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4871342Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4872156Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4872655Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4873113Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4874010Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4874685Z ```
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4874926Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4875172Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4876095Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4877195Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4878305Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4879419Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4880619Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4881427Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4881641Z ### Notes
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4881926Z 
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4882634Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4884196Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4885595Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4886986Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4888308Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4889555Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4890652Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-25T03:26:45.4891638Z </mcp-clis>
